newsitem.title: USA: Six survive mid-air plane collision in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Six survive mid-air plane collision in Florida.

text.p: Two single-engine planes collided in mid-air near Tampa but the pilots managed to land the damaged aircraft safely, aviation officials said Monday.
All six people aboard the two airplanes walked away from the collision but the aircraft sustained "major structural damage," authorities said.

"Mid-air collisions are rare. People who survive them are even rarer," said Susan Lane of the Hillsborough Aviation Authority, which owns the airport. "If they (the pilots) weren't trained so well they never would have survived."
The airplanes, a Beechcraft and a Cessna, collided Sunday at about 900 feet above tiny Vandenberg Airport near Tampa, the Hillsborough Sheriff's Office said.

The Cessna had just taken off and was banking into its flight pattern when it collided with the Beechcraft, which was coming in for a landing. Despite perfect weather, the two pilots apparently did not see each other, officials said.

The Beechcraft, piloted by Thomas Crowley, 55, of Tampa, lost its nose landing gear and part of the propeller. Crowley suffered a gashed foot when part of the fuselage crumpled into the cabin, but his passengers were not injured.

The impact of the collision left the Cessna's right aileron, which controls stability, stuck in the up position -- usually enough to cause a plane to roll over, officials said. But the tip of the plane's left wing also was damaged, apparently in a way that balanced the aircraft and allowed pilot Mark Thiem, 39, to land it safely.
